findings.title: A stranger's 5 ₳ at a KEY address whose hash is a pool's mix_box script hash counts as a pool box: it counts toward the floor, gets drawn, and every chain that draws it fails, so returns come back directly
findings.scenario: A stranger pays exactly the box value (5 ₳ for v2's 5 ₳ pool) to an enterprise KEY address (header 0x60 on preprod, 0x61 on mainnet). Its 28-byte key hash is the pool's mix_box SCRIPT hash M. The output carries the inline datum Constr 0 [a, b], with a = [r]G and b = [s]G: valid, not the identity, and a ≠ b. No key hashes to M, so the 5 ₳ is burnt for good. The contract never treats this UTxO as a box: input_at_script and output_at_script require Script(M). The wallet does. Koios's credential_utxos for M lists it beside the real boxes, with payment_cred = M; Koios matches the hash, whatever its kind. PoolBox::from_row compares only that string and the value, so the fake becomes 'a box a mix may take'. It joins `others`, which the floor counts as 'real boxes that aren't ours', and it is drawn like any other box. Any mix that draws it fails in the wallet's own measure: uplc's phase one finds a Spend redeemer on a key-locked input (RequiredRedeemersMismatch). fan_out never draws again. The runner's buildBack catches the error, sets sess.skip.warn.chainFailed, and sends the session's money back directly, with no review for a swap's return or a tile Mix's session. privacy.md:404 says that ties the session to the private UTxOs that paid for it. A tile Mix's funding and return fees are paid and nothing is mixed. The collateral's tail drops back to the rest. Mix my boxes again and the public mix fail at build. Odds, at Settings' default depth 2 and width 3 (8 fresh draws a box), with 60 real others: 5 fakes (25 ₳ burnt) let a 1-box return mix 51% of the time, a 2-box one 23% and a 4-box one 3%. 10 fakes (50 ₳) give 27%, 6% and 0.1%. The fakes can never be spent, so the effect lasts until a release changes the check, for every Seedelf Wallet user of that pool. This holds on preprod and wherever the pool is read from Koios: mainnet with the Koios-only switch, or while the data layer's private part is down. Whether mainnet's default data-layer route serves such rows depends on seedelf-data (see notes).

findings.evidence:
1. Rows. lovejoin.ts:3269 `this.deps.koios(network).credentialUtxos(ask.map((p) => p.mixBox))`. koios.ts:803-816 documents it: 'Every UTxO whose payment credential is one of `credentials` (key or script hashes, hex)'. The data layer path, lovejoin.ts:3254, uses `credOf = (r) => this.keysOf({ bech32: r.address }).cred`. keysOf (6345-6356) takes `kind < 8 ? hex.slice(2, 58)`, any header 0-7, key or script. private-index.ts:396 then forces `payment_cred: paymentCred` on every index row. The multi-pool Koios answer (3275) is kind-blind too.
2. seedelf-core/src/lovejoin/mod.rs:414-427 from_row: `if !protocol.box_value().is_row(row) || row.payment_cred != hex::encode(protocol.mix_box_hash) { return None; }`, then parse_mix_datum, then `eval::resolve_row(row).ok()?`. resolve (eval.rs:117+) is `Address::from_bech32(&row.address)` with no kind check. points() passes. value.rs:66-82 is_row compares the value only.
3. wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:2605-2622 owned_in partitions from_row's boxes into ours and `others`/`other_boxes`. lovejoin.ts:3336-3340: `// What the floor counts: real boxes that aren't ours and aren't spent. others: otherBoxes...`. draws (lovejoin.rs:369-375) filters only the wallet's own.
4. mod.rs:2509-2535 fresh_for shuffles every other box. fan_out (2546-2590) pops width−1 a mix and calls `mix(params, protocol, &inputs, &paying, rewards)?` (2574), with no redraw on failure.
5. mix_with adds `add_spend_redeemer` for each box input (mod.rs:1081) and measures with `eval::evaluate(...)?` (1139-1145). eval.rs:334-341 calls `uplc::tx::eval_phase_two_raw(..., true, ...)`, so run_phase_one is on. In uplc 1.1.23, tx.rs:71-73 runs eval_phase_one. phase_one.rs:77-82 lists a spend as needing a script only for `ShelleyPaymentPart::Script(h)`. has_exact_set_of_redeemers (198-272) then returns `RequiredRedeemersMismatch { extra: ["Spend[i]"] }`. eval.rs turns that into `bail!("The wallet couldn't evaluate the transaction: {e}")`.
6. sessions.ts:4655-4681: `chain = await lovejoin.chain(...)` inside try, `catch (e) { skipped = leftOut(e); }`. leftOut (6339-6344) gives `sess.skip.warn.chainFailed`. The direct return is then built. bringBack (4324-4334) sends it with no review: the runner's path for swaps and mix sessions.
7. The contract side, Lovejoin 29573c5 lib/lovejoin/mixbox.ak: `input_at_script ... Script(script_hash) -> script_hash == mix_script_hash; _ -> False`, and output_at_script also pins Script with no stake part and no reference script. cb5a5a3 is the same. On chain, a key-M UTxO is never a box.
8. privacy.md:405: 'the wallet draws from a pool only once it holds 30 real boxes that aren't the wallet's'. privacy.md:404: off Lovejoin, a session's ADA comes back 'tied on chain to the session and, through its funding, to the private UTxOs that paid for it'.

findings.title: A UTxO at a KEY address whose hash is the Seedelf contract's, under the user's register, counts in the private balance, and any spend that takes it fails: Max always fails for wallets of up to 20 private UTxOs
findings.scenario: A stranger takes a register from any of the user's Seedelfs (its datum is public) and re-randomizes it, (g^d, u^d). They pay about 1.34 ₳ (the least that output must hold) to an enterprise KEY address whose key hash is the contract's script hash, 94bca9c0…a469, with that register as the inline datum. Nobody can spend it, so the stranger's 1.34 ₳ is burnt. Koios's credential_utxos for the contract lists it, since it matches the hash, so the scan reads it. ownedUtxos checks only the register, so the private balance shows +1.34 ₳ that can never move. check_spendable passes it too (owned, no Seedelf, evaluable). Every Seedelf spend that takes it fails in the wallet's local measure, with uplc's phase-one RequiredRedeemersMismatch, the same mechanism as x2#1. Max picks a part's 20 inputs by worth. A wallet with 20 or fewer private UTxOs puts the row in its only part, so Max (Send all, Make public all) is refused outright in uplc's words. A larger wallet's Max sends the other parts and leaves the rest, giving the wrong reason. A payment of an amount fails only when its selection needs that UTxO: `apart` routes around a Failed choice where it can, and otherwise ends in the evaluator's words rather than 'not enough'. The way out is to lock that UTxO in coin control, if the user can tell which one it is. The CLI reads the contract the same way: `balance` counts the UTxO, and a transfer or sweep that takes it is refused by Ogmios.
findings.since: 58aff03b (2026-09-23, ownedUtxos) and 9faa02eb (check_spendable); in every release (first tagged web-wallet/1.6.0)
findings.evidence:
1. contract-scan.ts:148 `koios.credentialUtxos([contract.walletContractHash], after)`. koios.ts:803-816 documents it: 'key or script hashes'. The index path, contract-scan.ts:229, uses utxoOf with a forced payment_cred (private-index.ts:396).
2. balances.ts:489-506 ownedUtxos: `const hex = registerOf(utxo); ... return keys.seedelf.isOwned(register);`. Nothing reads utxo.address. contract-scan.ts:160 and 251 call it for every batch.
3. wasm lib.rs:2316-2343 check_spendable checks only ownership, the Seedelf policy and eval::refusal. Seedelf spends measure locally (lib.rs:2363 `spend.measure_locally(&[])`). resolve (eval.rs) keeps the row's key address, so uplc phase one (phase_one.rs:77-82, 198-272) refuses the extra Spend redeemer, as in x2#1 step 5.
4. Max: wasm lib.rs:4478-4489 calls fit_part. fit_part's `Err(_) => None` (4073) returns the error. max_in_parts then sets `failed = Some(e); break`, and `if !went && parts.is_empty() { return Err(e); }` (4535-4537).
5. Amounts: build.rs:2535-2581 select_script_inputs → apart (2660-2870). A Failed try is skipped (one_more), breaks the class (step 2) or abandons the order (grow → Grown::Failed). When nothing builds, the evaluator's error is returned.
6. The way out: coin-control.ts:3-5, 'A locked UTxO is left out of everything that spends that side, Max included'.
7. The CLI: seedelf-core/src/utxos.rs:32-53 collect_all_wallet_utxos and 111+ collect_wallet_utxos filter by `is_owned` alone.
findings.fix: The same class and fix as x2#1. Take a contract row only when its address's payment part is a SCRIPT with the contract's hash. Check it in the wasm check_spendable and in core's collect_* (CLI). In the worker, either drop rows whose header nibble is even before ownedUtxos, or let the wasm ownership call refuse them. Test (verifier, wasm): a contract row at ShelleyAddress::new(Testnet, Key(wallet_contract_hash), Null) under a re-randomization of the test key's register. Today it is owned, and a transfer that takes it errs with RequiredRedeemersMismatch. It should not be owned.
findings.known_check: The same searches as x2#1. Also searched backlog.md and archive/plans for 'Max' with 'evaluate', and for 'RequiredRedeemersMismatch' and 'extraneous': nothing. guards.stops: A row with a reference script or a datum too deep to read reaching an evaluated spend (unpriced fee, or a WebAssembly stack trap); every Seedelf spend, merged return and Lovejoin builder filters on it

run_phase_one = true: uplc's phase-one redeemer check refuses a transaction whose redeemers don't match its script inputs before it is signed. This is why x2#1 and x2#2 end as refusals, never as signed transactions the node refuses
A spent input's reference script that can't be measured counted as 0 bytes: a short fee the node refuses
A stranger's three UTxOs of 2^63-1 of one token making every spend's token total overflow: fitting leaves them out
Drawing a pool row that isn't exactly the box value (anyone mixing it would take the excess). The kind of its credential isn't checked (x2#1)
A Seedelf spend paying with a row that isn't the key's, holds a Seedelf, or the evaluator can't take. The address kind isn't checked (x2#2)
A stranger's identity, small-subgroup or non-canonical register counted as the user's (E6 checked the point rules)
A stranger's reference-script or deep-datum UTxO at a session account breaking the merged return: it becomes the plain sweep, which runs no script and pays for the bytes
A session account's UTxO whose reference script can't be measured stopping the return: it is left behind ('script') and the rest comes back
A stranger's odd token beside a swap's fill riding into a token pool's deposit on the user's ADA (fillsOf)
A stranger's UTxO at a DEX order's address taken for a partial fill of the session's own order (remnantsFrom follows it back to the order)
An input carrying the user's stake key under a stranger's payment key read as the user's public account in a box's origin (the stake key alone never counts)
An order output read as a script's unless its payment part is a script: the one kind-aware credential read among the readers traced
A chain or tail drawing the wallet's own boxes as others'

checked_ok: Lovejoin v2 (29573c5) and classic (cb5a5a3) output_at_script pin each mix output to the stake-less mix_box with no reference script, and walk_outputs pins the exact value and hashes the canonical datum. A stranger's mix can change only a box's datum spelling (r3a#1), never its stake part, a reference script, its value or what the proofs bind.

A stranger's copy of the user's (a, b) at the real mix_box carrying a reference script is hidden by eval::refusal inside PoolBox::from_row's resolve_row. It is invisible to the wallet and the stranger's own money, with no harm to the user.

Every evaluated spend filters rows with reference scripts or unreadable datums before selection: select_script_inputs (build.rs:2553), max_inputs (2911), the Lovejoin builders (wasm lovejoin.rs 445, 544, 1032, 2227 and others), session_collateral and plan_return. Plain account sends price a spent input's reference script (build.rs:567, 1015) and refuse one they can't size (utxos.rs:354-370).
Token totals from a stranger's rows: fitting leaves out what would overflow a u64, core resolve checks each row's sums, and TS sums in BigInt (chain.ts sumValue).

Public-account rows are matched by payment key hash (account.ts:121), so base with a foreign stake part, pointer and enterprise under the user's key are read and spendable. No one can make a script hash to a key hash, so the opposite confusion can't happen there.

Session-account rows are matched by the session key's hash (sessions.ts:2821, 5637). Every shape under that key comes back, a stranger's stake part included. Only the session key can be behind that hash.

The restore scan's `there` filter (sessions.ts:2954) is sound despite matching payment_cred: no one can spend a key row under the contract's hash, so any spent row with that credential is the script's.
madeBy never makes an input an account's by its stake key alone (lovejoin.ts:6236-6262). `mixed`/`mixedIn` match on payment_cred, but a key-M input can never be spent, so that can't be abused.

DEX: remnantsFrom takes a UTxO at an order's address only when it is traced back to the session's own order, and fillsOf keeps a stranger's odd token out of deposits. orders.rs order_at reads the credential's kind.

W1b's direct_tail pointer holds as written: the first exact 5 ₳ row is taken as the session's collateral. A stranger's 5 ₳ standing in becomes the user's box (a gift), and the session's own 5 ₳ comes back as change. No money is lost. The privacy cost is marginal next to a direct return's rest, and the stranger pays 5 ₳ each time.
Seedelf names are paid by full token name only (seedelf-name.ts), so a stranger's same-tag Seedelf can't redirect a payment. A handle's holder at a script address is refused by payable_address.
notes: r3a#1 family, a new fact for the fix: the TypeScript register reader (extension chain.ts:94, `pair.arg !== 2`) has the same rule as seedelf-koios register_of_datum (koios.rs:366, `d.array() != Some(2)`). Both refuse 102 with an indefinite pair, which r3a-1's verifier showed the node accepts. E6 holds the two readers to the same shapes, so a fix that widens one must widen both, and the TS copy is easy to miss. This only hides a payer's own money (low).

e1a#1 sibling: a key-M fake (x2#1) that copies the user's own box (a, b) is read as the user's box of unknown making. Through e1a#1's mechanism it is held as unmixed, and Mix my boxes again takes it first, so that chain can never build (phase one) while the fake exists. The way out is Bring one back by hand on the real boxes. Same fix as x2#1.
w2#2's class, traced past the window: the same kind-blind hash match reaches the private balance (x2#2) and the Lovejoin pool (x2#1). The one kind-aware reader of a credential is orders.rs order_at.

For the owner (seedelf-data, outside the chunk, not read): chunk-26-data-layer.md:479 says the private index reads db-sync through `idx_address_payment_cred`, and db-sync's address.payment_cred holds key and script hashes alike (address.has_script tells them apart). If the builder doesn't filter has_script, mainnet's default route serves key-H/key-M rows too, and x2#1 reaches every mainnet user, not only the Koios paths. Kupo's credential pattern (the fallback) is worth the same check. The wallet-side fix makes either moot.

To look up for x2#1/x2#2's Koios step (no network calls were made): koios-artifacts files/grest/rpc/address/credential_utxos.sql filters on payment_cred = ANY(...) with no has_script condition, as I recall it. Alternatively, on preprod pay 5 ₳ to addr_test1v<mix_box hash> and ask credential_utxos for that hash. koios.ts:803-806 already documents the endpoint as matching 'key or script hashes'.

W3's doubt on swap fills holds as stated: the direct return's `own` (sessions.ts:4553, passed at 4763) lacks `auto.fills`, so a fill's token UTxO is a stranger's to plan_return and comes back only if its own ADA pays its way. DEX fills normally carry about 2 ₳, which covers a register output. A DEX that returns tokens with only the key address's minimum would leave them at the one-time account. That is not traced to a real DEX, so no finding.

x2#1 grading: graded medium as a stranger-forced privacy downgrade plus lost mix fees, permanent and pool-wide for 25-50 ₳ burnt. The owner may weigh it higher. No funds are stranded, which the brief's high requires.
